= Appendix: Requirements
:toc:
:sectnums:

== Current approved next release — C 0.8.0

Product decision *V080-C-AND-V100-MULTIHOST-001* fixes the next release as
*0.8.0 dedicated to C, before Python*, and defers *multi-host qualification to
1.0.0*. The link:../adr/0009-supreme-multilanguage-v1-roadmap.adoc[accepted ADR 0009 amendment]
records authority; link:../releases/v0.8.0-plan.md[the bounded C plan]
records the 17 actionable work rows and acceptance criteria. This appendix owns
integrated status; the long-range link:../releases/v1.0.0-plan.md[roadmap] retains
all target languages and their relative order, with later version numbers
explicitly unassigned rather than silently renumbered.

[[c17-linux-review-candidate-2026-11-20]]
The *C17 Linux review candidate* captured on 2026-11-20 was built from
source revision `cb6e188231c1bbbbe83ff6f96fb7747df71dce65` for Linux
x86-64. The selected C04–C15 packaged matrix passed 319 cases, including 24
read-only navigation cases and 48 C06 local-binding cases. The C06 report
reconciliation preserves the runner exit and checks the archived protocol
traces, source digests and independent Clang controls. Separate C02 and C03
packaged results cover the toolchain, processes and compilation model.
The link:../releases/v0.8.0-progress.md#linux-candidate-verification--2026-11-20[completion register]
links the results and identifies the archive.

The two permanent context goldens await separate numeric overrides under
AGENTS §18.6. Full final-source regression, same-platform hosted CI,
independent review of distribution, and draft and public download
verification remain open. Other hosts remain *NOT VERIFIED* for 0.8.0.

[[c17-pinned-producer-authority-2026-11-18]]
*C17 pinned producer authority (2026-11-18):* the existing release-binding Story
vocabulary is reused for six producer-authority cases. Five original runs bound
evidence despite changed/missing/stale/forged/receipt-selected producer authority;
the positive lacked a producer binding. The retained RED archive is not a
framework failure. A focused Python application now prepares the existing Syft
1.42.3 from fixed official archive/executable/license hashes, accepts explicit
caller selectors, verifies the actual version/commit, and generates SPDX with
update checks and Java network access disabled. It bounds native execution,
output and payload input, compares the extracted tree with every archive member,
and publishes fresh evidence without overwriting caller files. It never runs the
upstream shell installer or selects an executable from an SPDX/producer receipt.

Source capture retains the selected executable/license/configuration identity;
final binding revalidates that identity, helper source, exact asset/payload/raw
SPDX hashes, generation receipt freshness and identity. Six cases/24 steps pass,
including actual native Syft generation over an authored metadata fixture. The
fixture's runtime placeholders are never executed and do not qualify a runtime
or release. Legacy metadata tests use a real producer but retain their original
report/refusal boundaries. Wider retained controls and actual workflow/native
asset replay are recorded separately, never inferred from these six cases.

Linux CI provisions the pinned producer before tests. Only the v0.8 release lane
delegates generation to the helper and requires the producer binding; the
historical v0.7 guarded blocks and sealed IDE provider remain unchanged. No new
framework, dependency version or global tool installation is introduced. The
eight-file slice and fresh four-step exact-reuse receipt are in
`.refactorkit/runs/c17-pinned-producer-authority-20261118-r001/`.
Actual CI, license review, independent review/download and full C01-C17/0.8.0
acceptance remain `actionable`. Work now prioritizes the existing IDE Java26/27
request without creating a duplicate requirement or promoting unqualified syntax.

[[c17-native-golden-authority-2026-11-16]]
*C17 native golden authority (2026-11-16):* exact Story
`REQ-C17-NATIVE-GOLDEN-001#c-golden-tests-require-native-compiler-authority-and-preserve-java-control`
establishes five C behavioral REDs and a passing Java control. Prefix goldens are
unknown to the old runner; two legacy include-order cases incorrectly pass

bounded owned UTF-8 fixture acquisition, explicit CLI Clang/clangd/formatter
selectors, portable workspace/compiler database tokens and declared C11/C17
argument-array contexts. It delegates preview/Apply to the C facade, compares
independent exact source images, verifies rollback and approval/journal state,
and records native qualification only on success. C never receives the generic
Java-JDT gate. Java follows its existing planner/diagnostics path.
Six cases/24 steps pass: two native positive goldens, missing-tool/context and
actual compiler-error refusals, plus Java control. Independent selected-Clang
oracles validate authored C inputs and reject the invalid fixture. A first Java
control used an unsupported one-line layout; the multiline control passes before
production changes. A first implementation supplied absolute inventory entries
to the relative owned-input reader; the reader correctly refused until the
adapter relativized them. Neither is hidden or counted as an additional product
RED. Existing C golden fixture migration and named native corpus, CLI/workflow
selectors, full C17 and release remain `actionable`; source tests do not qualify
a downloaded runtime. Evidence: `.refactorkit/runs/c17-native-golden-authority-r001/`.

The separately admitted permanent C11 and C17 prefix corpus now passes one
scenario/four steps per standard with independently authored source images and
selected-Clang syntax oracles. Same-prefix unrelated symbols, comments and string
literals stay unchanged. Evidence: `c17-prefix-c11-corpus-r001/` and
`c17-prefix-c17-corpus-r001/` under `.refactorkit/runs/`.
The original six-case authority/control Story is retained green after glue reuse.
Three legacy fixtures now declare exact C17 commands; extraction and standard
include ordering preserve their original positive images. The inline golden
still has a stale leading blank line in its expected image, while the native
renderer removes declaration and trailing whitespace. A ninth-file numeric
budget override is pending before that expected-image correction; no weakening

The two-TU component golden passes its persistent scenario/four steps with
exact native Apply/rollback and a root literal STATIC CMake target. Independent
Clang oracles compile both TUs before and after. Its original request and C
images remain unchanged; default selectors also register both prefix cases and
the historical scalar/include scenario. Fresh receipt and evidence:
`c17-legacy-relocate-golden-r001/green-r001/verification.json`.
Compiler databases intentionally remain unchanged after relocation: regeneration
is caller-owned, and the native gate evaluates the captured staged mapping.
CI's full golden command now receives all three paths from its verified native
bootstrap. The Testkit module passes 33 existing Java/model/discovery tests with
no skips/errors/failures (`c17-golden-testkit-regression-r001/verification.json`).
This is not a remote CI pass or native execution through the Gradle test alias.
The actual updated CI shell command executes the complete 32-request corpus

`c17-golden-ci-selectors-r001/verification.json` (123.1 seconds). The numeric
override is still pending; the complete command is not declared green.
Actual CI execution, complete corpus/operation coverage and current artifact,
runtime and release acceptance remain `actionable`.

== Annotated Java navigation correction

The earlier aggregate/status paragraphs are historical snapshots and do not include this addition.
The source of truth is link:../../features/java-annotated-member-navigation.feature[`REQ-JAVA-ANNOTATED-NAVIGATION-001`],
a functional, read-only CLI Business Need with one scenario, six declaration shapes and four steps.
Its declared status remains `@partial`: local Linux qualification does not certify every packaged platform
or every Java grammar shape, and does not change managed refactoring authority.

The bounded correction preserves inline/preceding/qualified/multiline annotation declarations and their
original source locations, including fields and constructors. `JavaLanguageAdapter.lookupSymbol` adds a
typed unavailable-analysis outcome while retaining the nullable `findSymbol` compatibility API.
The CLI keeps exit 1 and `Symbol not found` for missing selections; signed analysis with warnings now
returns exit 2, empty stdout and stderr code `java.definition.analysisIncomplete` with warning count and
first source diagnostic. Warnings are not ignored or reclassified as complete semantic evidence.
The default embedded image includes both `java.compiler` and `jdk.compiler` for `com.sun.source` consumers.

Validation uses the actual bundled launcher, an explicitly scrubbed environment and a disposable Maven
workspace. It checks exact declaration locations, compiler API availability, unrelated-error refusal,
recovery and unchanged input bytes. Run `:modules:refactorkit-cli:javaNavigationTest` with a JDK 21 build
JVM; the task builds the self-contained distribution and is part of `check`. The ordinary `test` task
excludes this package-dependent suite. Machine-readable results are written to
`modules/refactorkit-cli/build/reports/cucumber/java-annotated-member-navigation.json`.
The shared steps are thin adapters into the test-only navigation fixture; the pre-edit analyzer found
four required new steps and no reusable/ambiguous matches. This adds no new JUnit behavior test.

The external research and target-scoped concepts above were reviewed against RefactorKit base commit `c1d70fc51ef84fa25baaab5678dece69f8ce739a`; bounded implementation claims rely separately on dated mutable working-tree evidence. The 2026-07-30 clarification defines full-reactor graph completeness as descriptor-closed over selected nodes: every active reactor POM remains mandatory, every selected external node needs complete effective descriptor closure, and every outgoing declaration/classification is hash-bound. Bounded `010` validates the prune/alternate-selected-path boundary; bounded `011` independently validates the ordinary sidecar-free selected-`jar` row and its three under-lock drift gates; and six-case dual-classified outline `012` validates fail-closed `MISSING`, `MALFORMED`, and `DRIFTED` selected-descriptor outcomes with parsed relocation/model identity proof and stable recorded evidence. The follow-up Magrathea field observation is separately implementation-informed for consumer commit `a48e3c06` through the source-built CLI on Linux/JDK 21 after `010`; it is not architecture research promoted into a requirement, did not require `011` or `012`, and does not establish integration/native-matrix or general qualification.

The LATE REQ-JAVA-MAVEN-MOVE-AUTH-003 review reconciles the corrected feature with actual implementation. Four isolated copies use the ordinary default scanner to exercise a readable source omitted after an effective primary Maven `testSourceDirectory` replacement, a readable system-path JAR whose strict evidence-manifest fingerprint differs, a recovered target use without syntax failure, and a materialized generated-root inventory mismatch owned by `catalog-generated-support:main`. The effective model keeps primary main/test directories separate from additive build-helper/Kotlin roots: replacing a primary directory removes only the corresponding default Java root, while additive declarations retain defaults, and no plugin is executed. The two strict format-version-1 expected inventory manifests are snapshot-bound auxiliary files; blocker evidence carries manifest content hashes, and the classpath row carries expected/observed artifact fingerprints. Repeat guidance values and JSON are deterministic and schema/checklist version 1; CLI `--apply` refuses as `guidance.nonManaged` before `PatchEngine`, lock, or WAL. On 2026-07-30, the independent final OpenJDK 21 `./gradlew --no-daemon --rerun-tasks check goldenTest` run reported `BUILD SUCCESSFUL` in 7m 13s: 956 discovered, 773 executed, 183 skipped/tag-filtered, zero failures/errors, and 77 tasks executed; reviewed log SHA-256: `8d9b19576a27deaae2c12c767f929664c228db85d1dcc8644de3e41ecbe6ca9d`. This is dated mutable working-tree evidence; SpotBugs retained the configured non-blocking baseline findings. The REQ-003 implementation claim remains bounded to the Java dispatcher/source-built CLI; REQ-004 separately owns lexical review, and implemented REQ-008 separately owns its four uncertainty plus two refusal-phase cases.

The LATE REQ-JAVA-MAVEN-MOVE-AUTH-004 review reconciles the promoted feature with current implementation. `JavaMoveClassOperationDispatcher` is the direct Java move-class operation API: `Plan` may carry managed, refused, or result-owned typed structural-refusal results and rejects lexical evidence; `Guidance` carries REQ-003 plus four bounded REQ-008 preview uncertainties; and `LexicalReview` carries REQ-004 alone. This is not generic `LanguageAdapter` direct-apply evidence, and the cross-surface evidence in this paragraph belongs only to REQ-004. Schema-v1 reports `NOT_SEMANTICALLY_PROVEN`/`REVIEW_ONLY`/`LEXICAL_FALLBACK`/`INELIGIBLE`/`evidence.insufficient`, deterministic request/exact-snapshot/hidden-review-artifact/evidence SHA-256 identities, and `lexical-review-<sha256>` non-capability identity. The hidden artifact hash commits to internal compatibility file-operation paths, exact edit ranges, and replacement/create bytes; exposed records are only bounded normalized path/current-content-hash/typed-risk identities with `managedEdit=false`, `COMPLETE or TRUNCATED` record completeness, deterministic returned-category counts, and fixed next actions. CLI/protocol projections contain no plan/edit/range/replacement/apply token; recipe stops without an aggregate; daemon/LSP/MCP use lifecycle-cleared envelope-only LRU correlation; and shared exactly-one apply-identity parsing distinguishes known-operation structured `evidence.insufficient` from unknown/evicted `INVALID_PARAMS`. Daemon/LSP preserve JSON-RPC error `data`; MCP returns structured error content. The dedicated OpenJDK-21 report discovered 22 cases, executed/passed the one 38-step REQ-004 case, skipped 21, and had zero failures/errors; reviewed log SHA-256 `5fb89c290bd098f249c2ec734c8c7bbffae162e5357ab6b1683042fc68e698ce`. The test also preserves clean JDT managed-plan behavior and exact non-mutation. This is source-built/in-process evidence, not packaged/runtime/native qualification.

The LATE REQ-JAVA-MAVEN-MOVE-AUTH-008 review reconciles the corrected feature with current production/test code. Four complete preview uncertainties return immutable schema-v1 `JavaMoveClassReviewOnlyGuidance` with typed layers/codes for inside-closure ambiguity, unresolved static wildcard lookup, outside-closure explicit old FQN with closure precedence, and same-`S0` before/staged diagnostic identity drift; the last is collected by the dispatcher's second stage. None of those four returns `LexicalReview`, plan, or edit, and source-built CLI apply refuses `guidance.nonManaged` pre-`PatchEngine`/lock/WAL/residue. Missing root-declared `catalog-shipping/pom.xml` returns result-owned typed `JavaMoveClassStructuralRefusal`; deterministic component-wise workspace-relative `NOFOLLOW` identity supports a missing module directory and distinguishes it from a missing final POM, while symlink/non-regular states are not `MISSING`; source-built CLI refuses pre-lock/no-residue. The final case starts from eligible REQ-007 and binds one non-managed `BOUND_OTHER` source through immutable `OperationAuthorityFileEvidence`. `PatchEngine` captures one under-lock observed engine snapshot `S1`; immutable `DiagnosticDetails` reports primary `authorityLease.evidenceDrift` plus secondary `snapshot.scopeChanged` before WAL, preserving external `S1` and possibly the lock file. The semantic candidate-inventory hash is expected-only; expected/observed hashes describe required-file evidence, and no observed semantic inventory is claimed. All six remain independent of REQ-003/004/010/011/012. Surface evidence is limited to the source-built library and CLI for the five preview-time rows, and to library/`PatchEngine` acceptance for the under-lock row; no REQ-008 recipe/daemon/LSP/MCP parity is claimed.

== Java/Maven Move-Class Apply Authority Epic

This architecture integration summarizes the reviewed requirement without replacing specialist evidence. Accepted ADR 0012 distinguishes global source-set authority from narrower target-scoped Maven `moveClass` authority. The feature contains exactly thirteen implemented-and-validated definitions and 31 cases. Bounded `001`-`012` retain their meanings; `013` adds nine complete/edit-exact lock-held pre-WAL admission cases. No general Maven authority is inferred. The exact Magrathea `a48e3c06` request remains separately CLI/Linux/JDK-21-qualified. Public REQ-001 and the complete production-JAR matrix are validation modes rather than new catalogue entries. Exact revision-bound run `31336067318` passed both modes on four hosts; every native row is `PASSED` after independent promotion review.

=== LATE REQ-004 Implementation Evidence

Status: implementation-informed and reconciled with scenario-level `@implemented-and-validated`.

The corrected feature now uses the returned non-capability `operationId` for known daemon/LSP/MCP refusal and keeps arbitrary `planId=plan-lexical` as unknown input. Current source implements exactly-one non-blank `operationId`/`planId` parsing in core. A cached operation returns typed `evidence.insufficient`; no/both/blank, unknown/evicted operation, and arbitrary plan identities return `INVALID_PARAMS`. Daemon and LSP preserve blocker/envelope in JSON-RPC error `data`; MCP returns equivalent `isError=true` structured content.

The schema-v1 envelope is immutable and reports `NOT_SEMANTICALLY_PROVEN`, `REVIEW_ONLY`, `LEXICAL_FALLBACK`, `INELIGIBLE`, and `evidence.insufficient`. It binds normalized request, exact snapshot, hidden review artifact, and sorted evidence with four SHA-256 identities and deterministic `lexical-review-<sha256>` correlation. The exposed residual records are path/content-hash/risk identities with `managedEdit=false`, not source ranges or token hashes. Only `reviewArtifactSha256` commits to exact internal compatibility edit ranges and replacement/create bytes. Record bounds are 200 and 262,144 canonical UTF-8 bytes, with `COMPLETE or TRUNCATED`, total/returned counts, deterministic returned-risk-category counts, and four fixed next actions.

The direct API under test is `JavaMoveClassOperationDispatcher.preview` and its `JavaMoveClassOperationOutcome.LexicalReview`, not generic `LanguageAdapter.applyRefactoring`. CLI, recipe, daemon session, managed LSP session, and MCP session route Java `moveClass` through that boundary. No envelope exposes a plan/edit/range/replacement/apply token; no pending plan or LSP edit is created; recipe returns no aggregate; the bounded envelope-only LRU cache is lifecycle-cleared; compatibility-plan core apply refuses before lock/WAL; and a fresh clean JDT scan retains existing `SEMANTIC_PREVIEW`/`JDT_BINDING`/`ELIGIBLE` plan behavior.

The dedicated OpenJDK-21 Cucumber report discovered 22 cases, selected/executed/passed the single REQ-004 production case with 38 expanded steps, skipped 21 cases by tag filter, and recorded zero failures/errors. The reviewed focused log SHA-256 is `5fb89c290bd098f249c2ec734c8c7bbffae162e5357ab6b1683042fc68e698ce`; the final dry-run also discovered 22, selected one, skipped 21, and had zero failures/errors, with reviewed log SHA-256 `40814182128d54c599522e84887c2fd8b51c422988daade149dd2b49b83a0a39`. This proves the source-built/in-process scenario only and does not qualify packaged executables, stdio/editor deployment, runtime distributions, native platforms, or general move authority.

[[maven-nested-module-directory-move-2026-11-21]]
=== Move a Maven module directory while preserving its GAV

`REQ-JAVA-MAVEN-MODULE-RENAME-001#move-a-module-into-a-nested-directory-preserving-gav`
covers a non-aggregating JAR named by a literal module entry in the sole root
aggregator. Supply workspace-relative `oldModuleDir` and `newModuleDir` in
`refactor.preview` with operation `renameMavenModule`. The nested move preserves
GAV when `newArtifactId` is omitted or equals the existing artifact ID. The
existing Maven model exposes the moved module at `components/library` with ID
`components:library`.

The planner updates the root module entry and rebases the moved POM's local
parent reference when the destination depth changes. It handles both an explicit
root-POM `relativePath` and the default Maven parent lookup. Preview is read-only.
Apply revalidates the staged reactor and diagnostics. For a nested move, it
removes the old module path from the workspace after the tracked file moves.
The journal retains the original directory tree so normal rollback restores
its hierarchy along with the saved files. Rollback reports a conflict when the
old path has been recreated. A POM edit at the source path precedes the file
move in the ordered work plan. The edited POM is installed at the destination.
Linked or blocked destination ancestors, overlapping module roots and
unqualified parent references refuse. Recovery of an interrupted Apply may
remove the conventional empty Maven output directories authorized in the
transaction journal after checking their identity. An unrelated path, a link,
a real generated file or an independent edit still requires manual resolution.

The daemon advertises `features.nestedModuleDirectoryMove=true` on the
`java.renameMavenModule` entry from `server.capabilities`. Consumers can use
this feature flag to gate nested destinations. Six library Story cases passed.
The packaged daemon passed preview, Apply, Maven 3.9.16 offline verification
with JDK 21 and exact rollback for both parent forms and the existing flat
artifact-rename control. Consumer POM bytes remained exact in the nested moves.
The Linux x86-64 archive SHA-256 is `4ab5b846afb8672498b9c938ca23487d4050a0a4f736c36fc69a51a12c62e8da`.
Evidence is retained under
`.refactorkit/runs/v080-ide-maven-module-nested-directory-20261121-r001/`.

[cols="1,4",options="header"]

|Dimension |Accepted scope

Module groupId mutation; module version mutation; dependency type/classifier other than jar/empty; duplicate occurrences beyond one exact literal; parent-coordinate migration; nested/profile modules; module creation; packaging changes; JPMS; move to another aggregator; property/inherited origins. No new CLI/JSON-RPC/LSP/MCP protocol schemas; no recipe composition/authority; recipe-private whole-package `movePackage` is not public; no packaged/native-host/cross-platform qualification; no general Maven projects; no disposable real-project qualification; no green whole-repository/release result; no I1 checksums/SBOMs/attestations/download verification; no `formatFile`/createMavenModule/external-import/Kotlin/TypeScript; no recursive package migration; no configuration/framework-string rewriting; no hierarchy restructuring beyond the two explicit refusal rows (`N-PULL-UP` -> `java.hierarchy.pullUp.unsupported`, `N-PUSH-DOWN` -> `java.hierarchy.pushDown.unsupported`).

|Non-functional. The scenario constrains compatibility, separation of concerns, protocol stability, and authority/lifecycle ownership.

[cols="2,5",options="header"]
|===
|Policy boundary |Surface-owned decisions

== Java Refactoring Preview Command Boundary

Status: implementation-informed and reconciled with feature-level `@implemented-and-validated`. `features/java-refactoring-preview-command-boundary.feature` has no `Background`; one five-row `Scenario Outline` and three ordinary scenarios produce four repository-unique non-functional definitions, eight cases, 46 declared scenario steps, and 94 expanded steps. Production evidence is `JavaRefactoringPreviewCommand.kt`: a sealed hierarchy containing only `RenameClass`, `RenameMember`, `MoveSourceRoot`, single-file `OrganizeImports`, and `SafeDelete`; a fieldless `JavaRefactoringPreviewDispatcher`; an internal per-call `JavaRefactoringPreviewPlannerInvoker` seam; and `ExistingJavaRefactoringPreviewPlannerInvoker`, which maps to the unchanged default planners. Five generic `JavaLanguageAdapter` decoders converge on the dispatcher. Daemon and MCP construct only these five commands after their existing parsing/required-field checks; their refused-plan, pending-plan, and rendering policies remain outside.

The pre-implementation baseline passed Java 245/245, daemon 58/58, and MCP 26/26 on OpenJDK 21.0.11 (log SHA-256 `46a52ccf5fb116f5f52c7b116947ade4ff8faceea0d2fa999c330cc5cc4f1560`). The absent API produced a meaningful compile RED (SHA-256 `3221bc7bc6aaef1a21117032ce6f22ea7c28ea8efb05a2797e2fec1beb3b5af8`). The first independent review correctly blocked promotion because REQ-003 was source-only. The correction reused the same feature through split runners: the Java-module runner executes REQ-001/002/004 with sentinel plus real default planners; the CLI-module runner executes REQ-003 through public `DaemonSession`/`McpSession` dispatch, covering all five operations plus missing, unknown, and refused paths and no preview writes/residue. Final focused evidence passed seven Java scenarios/85 steps plus one real-surface scenario/9 steps—four definitions, eight cases, 94/94 steps—with zero failures/errors (log SHA-256 `10c805b67306026cb4ab4a79de9b7258c712e28aaf0bb0070279edbbc44914f5`; JSON SHA-256 `2059c28d57fde8f72b2e3f0de9fe6d95062c8de6cad40aeaeee3e4175a378ef6` and `999ee1a13d8577113113236e7b2241a5fac881e97327705eb1e4d1858ed83baa`). Independent regressions reported Java 253 discovered/252 executed/one tag-filtered, daemon 58/58, and MCP 26/26 with zero failures/errors (log SHA-256 `9a1cb587e7e377682a09353f470140a76e4dae1e5cb42a727f8ed346e2a0e9b1`).

== Transactionality Requirement Clarifications

These requirements capture the audit's required contract decisions and acceptance gaps. They are not implementation claims.

[cols="1,4,1",options="header"]
|===
|ID |Requirement |Status

|REQ-TX-001
|Define atomicity, consistency validation, isolation, durability, compensation, rollback, and crash recovery separately; do not describe current preflighted compensatable batches as ACID or crash-safe transactions.
|needs-review; release-blocking terminology

|REQ-TX-002
|Define the transaction boundary for one plan, recipe, native LSP edit, custom managed LSP apply, diagnostics, and direct library use.
|needs-review

|REQ-TX-003
|Cover process kill, power loss, disk full, permission change, non-atomic filesystems, log corruption, concurrent writers, and editor-buffer divergence in the failure model.
|planned acceptance

|REQ-TX-004
|Normal rollback must detect post-apply conflicts and refuse rather than silently overwrite later changes; forced and manual recovery require explicit contracts.
|planned release blocker

|REQ-TX-005
|Define a durable versioned journal lifecycle, integrity and permissions, retention, startup recovery, and observable incomplete-recovery states before managed writes are called crash-safe.
|planned release blocker

|REQ-TX-006
|Define snapshot scope, engine-verified affected-file preconditions, per-path expected hashes, metadata scope, case sensitivity, generated files, and symbolic-link behavior.
|planned release blocker

|REQ-TX-007
|Define authoritative diagnostics and regression gates before, during simulation, after apply, and after rollback, including deterministic recovery when validation fails.
|planned release blocker

|REQ-TX-008
|Define one-writer workspace locking, timeout, stale-lock recovery, cancellation, and multi-process behavior.
|planned release blocker

|REQ-TX-009
|Classify native LSP edits as client-managed/no-rollback, overlay full-sync buffers, require monotonic versions, emit exact open-document versions, refuse incapable clients, and guard managed disk writes from open-buffer divergence.
|implemented and tested (`TX-007` closed)

|REQ-TX-010
|Stage every recipe step against one evolving immutable snapshot, expose one recipe-wide plan, and perform at most one managed WAL transaction; planning failure and no-op execution must not write journal records.
|implemented and tested (`TX-008` closed)

|REQ-TX-011
|Use one coordinate space per file/plan, merge all same-file edits, validate complete line/character bounds and cross-edit overlap, and render every final file before mutation.
|planned release blocker

|REQ-TX-012
|Treat explicit managed apply as auditable approval, refuse missing authorization, persist approval identity, map managed refusal categories deterministically, and refresh integration state after mutation.
|implemented and tested (`TX-016`, `TX-017`, `TX-018` closed)
|===

== Validation Modes

[cols="1,3",options="header"]
|===
|Mode |Meaning

|Documentation evidence
|Behavior is described in repository docs or `AGENTS.md`.

|Source evidence
|Behavior appears in module source files.

|Unit test evidence
|Behavior has module tests.

|Golden test evidence
|Behavior has a `testdata/golden` case.

|CI evidence
|Behavior is exercised by `.github/workflows/ci.yml`.

|Domain research
|A reviewed requirement or concept informs planned architecture but is not repository implementation or executable evidence.

|Field report
|A dated external observation motivates priority and qualification; it does not replace a permanent fixture or prove general support.

|Gherkin source reconciliation
|Feature discovery, stable IDs, classifications, effective statuses, paths, totals, and architecture/use-case mappings agree with the `.feature` source. This validates documentation consistency only, not behavior or implementation.

|Tagged Cucumber evidence
|A runner filtered by a stable requirement tag executes the selected production scenario. Passing steps support only that scenario and exercised surface; scenarios reported skipped because of the filter remain unvalidated.

|Packaged-process Cucumber evidence
|A dedicated runner executes an existing tagged pickle through the real self-contained launcher and embedded runtime as child OS processes. It is a validation mode, not a new requirement/case. Exact revision-bound run `31336067318` passed public REQ-001 and the complete matrix on Linux x86-64, Windows x86-64, macOS x86-64, and macOS arm64. Each row remains independently `PASSED` until its exact receipt passes independent review; source-built, generic package, static-review, or local evidence cannot promote it.

== C02 Clangd Native Runtime Currency (2026-10-22)

`REQ-C-CLANGD-RUNTIME-CURRENCY-001` guards clangd with the same retained native
runtime identity used by discovery. A missing capture refuses before launch with
`c.clangdRuntimeUnavailable`; a changed identity, executable selector or runtime
object refuses with `c.clangdRuntimeChanged`. The guard runs before launch and
before/after document and semantic exchanges. A changed retained input closes the
owned clangd process and private launch context before the result can be used.

The six-case
link:../../features/c-compiler-runtime-currency.feature[clangd runtime Story]
uses actual private Clang 22.1.8. Its current control resolves the bound `adjust`
definition. Missing capture, changed identity, a substituted executable selector
and an exit-zero canary refuse before launch; changing the owned copied `libffi`
after launch revokes the query and reaps the process. All six examples pass. The
final hash-bound receipt, pre/post installed-analyzer inventories, selected
Cucumber JSON/XML and six case records are in
`.refactorkit/runs/v080-clangd-runtime-currency-r001/`.

The first test task selected zero examples because the shared runner's explicit
tag allowlist omitted this requirement identity. The runner now includes the
exact scenario tag; the recorded §18.6 override is thirteen changed files,
including its approval record. The pre-edit inventory had one effective runner,
zero ambiguity/duplicate groups, three new steps and one exact reuse. The post-edit
inventory has one runner, zero ambiguity/duplicate groups and four exact matches.
There is no per-slice runner, duplicate glue or new dependency.

Focused source-built regressions also pass: three `CCrashRecoveryTest` cases, one
native `ClangdSemanticIntegrationTest`, the six-case clangd launch-configuration
outline, and five separately selected timeout, cancellation, restart, concurrent
close and malformed-handshake Stories. This cell covers only native runtime
currency at clangd launch/query boundaries. Complete source/header/configuration
and host authority, filesystem replacement races, runtime preview leases and
post-commit checks remain `actionable`; full C02 and all C01-C17 acceptance remain
required. No release publication is claimed.

One additional exact-identity Story now covers client close while native runtime
admission is blocked. A delayed admission cannot launch clangd after close or

[[JavaM2ProjectContextReconciliation]]
=== M2 project-context acceptance reconciliation (2026-10-18)

M2 extends the existing source-built API 0.2 implementation; it is not a new
project-model implementation. The source build exposes daemon `project.context`
and `project.sync`. Maven acquisition uses the offline effective reactor model and
does not run Maven plugins. Ordinary Gradle discovery remains declarative/partial
and cannot establish authoritative source ownership. Explicit caller-authorized
Gradle `project.sync` evaluates the project offline under bounded execution and
output limits and exports effective context without requesting compilation or
annotation-processor tasks. It evaluates Gradle build scripts and plugin
configuration code; offline resolution is not a sandbox. Gradle or Maven remains
responsible for build, run and test lifecycle operations.

The public model carries module/source-set identity, source roots, materialized
generated roots, outputs, dependency declarations, ordered compile/runtime
classpaths, provenance and selected SDK/compiler evidence. The Maven and Gradle
fixtures are required to assert those fields, exact source association, provenance,
stale-POM/build/tool rejection, and agreement between the selected JDK, each
source-set compiler and the classpath consumed by JDT. Each source-set row pairs its
roots with its own compile/runtime classpaths; acceptance must prove no classpath
leakage across Maven profiles/modules or Gradle source sets. An unsynchronized partial
Gradle model must never supply source ownership. `docs/java-project-context-protocol.md`
owns the versioned request/result contract and currently implemented typed refusal
codes.

descriptor identity (`path`, `moduleName`, `open`, `requires`, `exports`, and the
descriptor content hash). The provider now treats every module directive other than
`requires` and `exports` as unprojected, marks JPMS `partial`, and refuses
`requiredFacts: [JPMS]` with `java.context.jpmsDescriptorIncomplete`. Its bounded
Maven Stories verify supported descriptor fields and the content hash while covering
both the real positive named-JAR case and `opens`, `uses`, and `provides`; a Gradle
Story verifies the corresponding positive module-path metadata. No new versioned
field was added. The positive cases assert exact module names and the
snapshot-bound file fingerprint. A second Story
changes `module-info.java` after snapshot capture and verifies the public route refuses
with `java.context.snapshotStale` before publishing module facts. A third changes a
compiler-configured Maven module-path JAR after open and verifies the same refusal.

`.refactorkit/runs/java-jpms-descriptor-completeness-r001/`,
`.refactorkit/runs/java-jpms-stale-descriptor-r001/`,
`.refactorkit/runs/java-jpms-stale-module-path-r001/`,
`.refactorkit/runs/java-jpms-positive-module-path-r001/`,
`.refactorkit/runs/java-jpms-gradle-positive-module-path-r001/`. The Gradle acceptance
found that compiler module-path artifacts were absent from scanner `ClasspathEvidence`;
the scanner now captures literal `JavaCompile.options.compilerArgs` module-path entries.
The stale-artifact Story changes that JAR after explicit sync and verifies the old
context refuses with `java.context.snapshotStale` before publishing module facts;
receipt `.refactorkit/runs/java-jpms-gradle-stale-module-path-r001/`.

[[JavaSemanticNavigationQueries]]
=== Compiler-bound Java type, call and implementation navigation

`intelligence.query` accepts `typeDefinition`, `typeHierarchy`, `callHierarchy`, and
`implementations` for Java. Queries bind a workspace-relative path and zero-based
UTF-16 position to the selected saved snapshot; SDK-bound immutable Java overlays
use the existing `javaContext` and closed-overlay authority path. JDT binding keys
identify the selected source type or method. No lexical fallback promotes unresolved
names to compiler evidence.

Type definition returns one workspace-source declaration. Type hierarchy supports
`supertypes`, `subtypes`, and `both`, with an explicit workspace-source scope and
bounded results. Call hierarchy supports `incoming` and `outgoing` direct JDT-bound
method and constructor invocations, grouped by source method with call-site locations;
its scope is `workspace-direct-invocations` and the response remains partial because
dynamic dispatch and method references are not modeled. Unresolved or external
relationships without a resolved JDT binding are omitted with incompleteness/warning
metadata. Resolved classpath-only methods remain as call-hierarchy targets grouped by
their exact JDT binding and JVM owner/name/descriptor, so overloads stay distinct.
Each item carries `methodIdentity`; `method` is null when no workspace source symbol
exists, and `sourceNavigation` explicitly reports that no classpath source location
is available. The top-level `targetScope` is
`workspace-source+resolved-classpath`; call sites remain workspace direct invocations.
Results retain the
snapshot/index identity, source authority, JDT provider, compiler evidence, and
provenance hash. The public response schema is
`docs/api-0.2-intelligence-query-schema.json`; Java authority details remain in the
bounded `docs/java-project-context-protocol.md` satellite.

The receipt-bound Maven dependency call-hierarchy Story validates overloaded targets
from a local system-scoped JAR without inventing source locations. Its companion
Gradle Story validates the same contract against an explicitly synchronized local
file dependency; neither Story executes dependency plugins or reaches remote
repositories. Both preserve the existing `REQ-JAVA-SEMANTIC-NAVIGATION-001`
requirement and navigation runner.

Implementation lookup accepts a source type or method declaration. For types it walks
the compiler-bound workspace inheritance graph and returns concrete class, enum or
record declarations, excluding abstract intermediates. For methods it follows exact
JDT override relations and returns concrete source method declarations; matching names
alone never create a result. The response distinguishes `targetKind`, reports
`scope: workspace-source`, and binds each result to the same JDT provider and
provenance. Recovered targets refuse. Missing bindings, analyzer warnings, or a
truncated result set set `complete: false` and `completeness: partial`; external
libraries and runtime-discovered implementations are outside this query's scope.

`REQ-JAVA-SEMANTIC-NAVIGATION-001` has one receipt-bound Story scenario covering all
four query kinds, concrete type/method results, bounded output and unresolved-target
refusal. The analyzer's pre-edit inventory found three exact step reuses and two new
steps; the post-edit inventory found five exact reuses, with no ambiguous/duplicate
expressions or runner ambiguity. The existing navigation runner remains the only
effective runner. `:modules:refactorkit-cli:javaNavigationTest` passes both selected
scenarios (9/9 steps).

`int` literal. The source and target may have no explicit hierarchy, generic
parameters, or interfaces, and the target hierarchy must have no same-named method.
All references must be complete JDT-bound direct invocations within that source
set; method references and callers outside the source-set closure refuse. Staged
rebinding runs against a temporary diagnostics overlay so the moved declaration
and updated callers are resolved from the same post-edit source image. New JDT
errors refuse the plan. The preview is HIGH risk, requires approval, and warns
that binary, reflective, external, framework-string, and resource-shaped
consumers are outside the proven reference set.

[[c-semantic-rename-target-collision-refusal]]
=== C06 conservative target-identifier collision refusal — 2026-10-22

The collision Story
`REQ-C-SEMANTIC-RENAME-001#header-selection-refuses-a-same-translation-unit-target-collision`
reproduced a gap: clangd returned a rename edit even though the requested
function name was already defined in the selected translation unit. The C
facade now checks the captured C-family source tokens before accepting a rename
proposal. If the target spelling occurs as an ordinary or unclassified
identifier token, it returns `c.renameTargetIdentifierPresent` with no workspace
edit, affected file, approval or transaction. The tokenizer excludes comments
and string/character literals; it never supplies replacement edits.

This is a conservative refusal boundary, not scope-aware proof that every
existing spelling conflicts. A same-spelled token in a safe, different scope
or lookup space may also be refused; the separately qualified tag-only C case
below is the sole current namespace exception. Full binding-aware collision,
shadowing and linkage analysis remains open for C06.

collision receipt and reports are in
`.refactorkit/runs/c-semantic-rename-collision-r001/`; the requalified prior

workspaces fell through to Clang with empty project flags. Because the default

native runtime. The database is parsed as data; only literal C11/C17, source,
`-c`, and bounded simple `-D` flags are admitted. Preprocessor directives,
include paths, targets, sysroots, output paths and other command arguments refuse
before Apply because their inputs are not modeled by this cell. Baseline and staged
syntax diagnostics cover every captured TU in the admitted project, introduced
errors refuse, and the transaction checks post-Apply diagnostics before success.
The Story confirms project input bytes are unchanged, no build output is created,
and rollback restores the exact source. Its hash-bound receipt, one-runner
inventories and execution reports are in
`.refactorkit/runs/c-format-managed-apply-r001/`. This is one bounded C07/C16
integration cell, not complete multi-TU/preprocessor C03/C05 authority; broader
flags, includes, ranges and filesystem race handling remain `actionable`.

The separate Story
`REQ-C-FORMAT-SOURCE-001#changed-captured-c-style-refuses-managed-apply-after-preview`
changes the captured direct `.clang-format` after preview. Managed Apply refuses
with `authorityLease.evidenceDrift`, preserves the source and external style
change, and creates no transaction journal. One C17 translation unit passes as
one scenario/three steps; the receipt, one-runner inventories and reports are in
`.refactorkit/runs/c-format-style-drift-apply-r001/`. This proves only selected
style-file drift detection in that bounded context. Other evidence-drift shapes,
multi-TU/preprocessor inputs, broad C07 qualification and C01-C17 release
acceptance remain open.

### Daemon request worker failure isolation

`REQ-DAEMON-REQUEST-ISOLATION-001` adds one bounded operational Story at
`features/daemon-request-error-isolation.feature`. A non-fatal `AssertionError`
from one request handler must produce JSON-RPC `INTERNAL_ERROR` and leave the
single scheduler worker able to answer the next queued request. The scheduler
rethrows `VirtualMachineError` and `ThreadDeath`; this does not claim recovery
from JVM-fatal conditions or reproduce the native IDE's unobserved query
failure. The focused Story and analyzer receipt are recorded under

steps; the complete daemon module suite passes 64 tests with no failures,
errors or skips. Broader daemon and native IDE qualification remain actionable.

[[c12-managed-inline-function-2026-11-12]]
=== C12 compiler-bound function inline — 2026-11-12

Status: bounded implementation verified locally; the wider C12 acceptance and
release qualification remain `actionable`. This appendix owns the integrated
architecture narrative. The executable behavior authority is
`features/c-inline-function-value-preservation.feature`, exact scenario
`REQ-C-INLINE-FUNCTION-EFFECT-001#captured-c-functions-inline-with-exact-semantics-approval-and-rollback`.

The C facade now delegates function inline to a native compiler planner and its
operation-specific managed gate. The first cell admits one internal static,
fully prototyped int function, one direct call, atomic int arguments, and one
straight-line int caller in a captured single-source C11/C17 compilation context.
Optional prototypes are resolved as the same declaration family and removed
with the definition. Parameter substitution follows compiler declaration IDs
and owned source spans; strings and other non-binding text are preserved.
Supported expression leaves include an in-bounds promoted character read from
an ordinary string constant. Conversions, effects, captured/global names,
additional function-value consumers, macros and unsupported declarations refuse.

Before and staged ASTs are normalized into typed value/binding images whose
identities exclude compiler process IDs and byte offsets. The independently
substituted expected caller image must equal the compiled staged image. The
lease retains both semantic digests, the edit and snapshot identities, native
runtime and resource identities. Managed apply rebuilds the preview authority
and rechecks before/staged/post-apply images. A caller-supplied disabled gate
cannot replace that authority. The old low-level structural planner remains a
proposal primitive; it is no longer the facade's managed inline-function path.

The six expanded Story cases pass in actual offline Gradle with the pinned
Clang 22.1.8 runtime: precedence and local arguments in C11/C17, a prototype
family and a string operand in C17. Each case includes missing approval, changed
source and forged semantic-lease refusals without a transaction, followed by
explicit apply, an independent exact image and exact rollback. A genuine RED
run failed all six on structural rather than compiler evidence. Receipts,
effective-glue inventories and reports are retained under
`.refactorkit/runs/c12-managed-inline-function-r001/` and its RED/GREEN siblings.
This is a narrow safety cell, not general C inlining, C++/Objective-C support,
whole-root/CI qualification or a completed 0.8.0 release.

The current full C module also passes 324 tests with no skips or failures,
including five new pure Kotest 5.9.1 specifications. Independent source-owned
AST oracles exercise process-independent binding identities, foreign same-name
declarations, unsupported conversions/effects, an escaped function value and
macro-owned spans. The full module XML archive and verification are retained
in `c12-managed-inline-function-r001/`; no new framework or dependency was added.

Documentation/surface gaps: `actionable` — qualify the remaining CLI/daemon/LSP/MCP
inline-function execution matrix. The former MCP `static/extern` description is
corrected by the separate C16 catalogue Story below; this does not imply support
for externally visible functions.

The existing five-case counterexample Story separately passes 20 steps using
the actual captured compiler, preserving both positive cases and all three
refusals. Its earlier two positive failures came from the old fictitious runtime
fixture, not an admitted semantic regression. The final shared-glue recheck of
the six managed cases passes 24 steps in
`.refactorkit/runs/c12-managed-inline-function-green-r002/`; the separate legacy

[[c03-owned-bounded-source-capture-2026-11-13]]
=== C03 owned and bounded structural source capture (2026-11-13)

Authority: REQ-C-SOURCE-CAPTURE-001#structural-capture-refuses-unowned-or-over-budget-source-inputs
is one seven-file filesystem-adapter Story with six examples and four thin new
steps, no dependencies or runner, and an unambiguous effective-glue inventory.
The regular-source control passes on the original scanner; five genuine RED
cases expose external file/root symlinks and unbounded file/aggregate/entry reads.
The first sandbox attempt fails before test execution and is not semantic RED.
Evidence: `.refactorkit/runs/c03-owned-source-capture-r001/`.

The scanner delegates source capture to a descriptor-relative no-follow reader.
Each root ancestor and visited directory is opened through SecureDirectoryStream;
source channels are opened relative to that handle without following links.
An unavailable provider, any non-ignored symlink, missing stable file identity,
non-regular selected source, changed observed identity, unreadable input or
invalid UTF-8 raises CProjectScanException with an explicit CProjectScanFailure;
no partial ProjectSnapshot is returned. Directory traversal and source reads
are streaming and bounded: 25,000 entries (including root), depth 64, 4,096
sources, 2 MiB per source and 64 MiB total source bytes. Callers may tighten these
limits. Shared snapshot ignored-directory names are excluded. C-family language
classification and sorted workspace-relative source paths remain structural;
no compiler or manifest command is executed.

All six native cases/twenty-four steps pass with unchanged source identities
and same-agent SHA/XML archive checks. This closes the observed stable
source-link read path in CProjectScanner. Ancillary capture still uses its existing independent policies;
this is not atomic whole-workspace evidence, comprehensive race qualification,
transport error-envelope qualification, an Apply bypass fix or full C03/C17.
Follow-up source-count/depth/UTF-8, ignored-tree and directory-link cases and
transport mapping remain actionable until their separate native evidence exists.

Metadata-only Java 26/27 context must not become semantic main discovery by inference.

scheduler cancellation, without late output or retained registrations.

planned extension. server.capabilities/schema/profile support must be published

[[java-declared-project-provider-2026-11-13]]
=== REQ-JAVA-PROJECT-CONTEXT-001: explicit plain-Java provider and exact source closures (2026-11-13)

Plain Java projects have a separate java-declared-v1 Build Model provider; the
conventional provider remains partial. The opt-in UTF-8 file
.refactorkit/java-project.json has schemaVersion=java-declared-project-v1,
absolute sdkHome and an explicit modules array. A module requires id, root and
sourceSets. Each source set requires id, kind (main/test/integration-test/custom),
sourceRoots, generatedSourceRoots, outputDirectories, compileClasspath,
runtimeClasspath, integer release and proc=none. No field is guessed or omitted.
Source/generated/output paths are normalized workspace-relative and contained in
the declared module root; source/module roots may use dot, normalized to an empty
workspace-relative root on the wire. Generated roots must also be source roots.
Classpath entries are explicit normalized relative/absolute paths, with preserved
order. IDs, roots and output ownership must be unique/unambiguous. Runtime and
compile classpaths are distinct; an output is not implicitly added to either.

The native compiler context uses selected roots first and adds another source set
only when its uniquely declared output occurs explicitly on compileClasspath.
There is no Maven main/test default, transitive dependency guess or frontend
semantic substitute. Compiler release/proc facts and source-root descriptor
provenance are complete for this declared format. Artifact coordinates remain
not-declared. The selected SDK must match the declaration's compiler home and its
attested platform identity; discovery never uses the engine runtime as project
SDK authority. Configuration changes invalidate snapshot/context tokens.
Java26/27 declarations cannot inherit semantic support from installed JDT: older
schemas refuse and v6/v7 use metadata only. This provider's metadata26/27 matrix
still needs independent qualification; installed SDK presence does not qualify it.

The provider adapter delegates to an application capture service and owned input
ports. Manifest JSON is closed, duplicate-key/nesting bounded and read through
no-follow owned handles. Classpath files/directories are captured with bounded,
no-follow readers producing the existing ENTRY fingerprint format; a positive
JAR/directory fixture checks equality with standard fingerprints. A classpath
input must exist unless it is a declared future output. Declared outputs may be
absent before Build. Existing Maven/Gradle descriptors conflict and never become
implicitly replaced, parsed for settings credentials or executed. Missing/invalid/
unsafe declarations and unavailable classpaths remain typed outcomes; absence of
the manifest preserves the conventional provider and missing-compiler refusal.
No build goal, annotation processor, network lookup or application main executes.

bounds are not a claim that every hostile/resource boundary has been exercised.
The same requirement/Story reuses four exact steps and the existing runner, with
no new step, duplicate expression, runner or production dependency. Eight changed

declared TU types. WG14's C11 committee draft
https://www.open-std.org/jtc1/sc22/wg14/www/docs/n1570.pdf[N1570,6.2.7 paragraphs1-2]

tag/member compatibility conditions across TUs. This is not established by two
separate successful syntax checks. The policy therefore requires consumer proof
before source mutation rather than certifying unknown external compatibility.

The public getBuildPath contract now supplies the adapter's standalone identity.

Evidence: .refactorkit/runs/c17-runtime-component-producer-20261119-r001/.
Main-tree replay passes six cases / 24 steps with explicit selection and again
with the normal default tag filter. Retained release and actual CLI/LSP task-model
controls pass 45 cases / 180 steps; all 2,033 source identities stay unchanged.
The discovery control reports 109 features / 1,337 expanded C cases with complete
runner/default-filter coverage, not full execution of that catalogue. Its first
replay caught the new filter operand using only a requirement prefix; replacing
that operand with the exact requirement#scenario identity restores coverage.
The original failure is retained; neither the discovery guard nor its expected
coverage is weakened. Main product capture also matches all 50 sealed JARs.
Authenticated binder rederivation, SPDX normalization, legal
review, full C01-C17 regression/CI and release/download remain actionable. The
completion register links to this appendix as integrated qualification authority.


[[c17-spdx-runtime-coordinate-reconciliation-2026-11-19]]
=== Gradle coordinates in SPDX

The SPDX qualifier compares the supplied Gradle manifest with the complete
application JAR inventory using each archive path, SHA-256 and SHA-1. It
replaces PURLs only when the source member and whole-JAR checksum identify
one upstream package. A JAR omitted by the cataloger receives its own
package record. License values and unrelated package records are retained.

The six-case Story verifies reconciliation, missing and changed components,
ambiguous detection, changed output and malformed coordinates. All 43
existing release controls passed. Replay of the sealed 6e6e candidate
verified 224 files and 50 resolved JARs, corrected 23 PURLs and recorded
javax.inject. The upstream document retains its original digest. Proof:
.refactorkit/runs/c17-spdx-runtime-coordinates-20261119-r001/.
Source authority and release qualification are covered separately.

For JNA and JNA Platform 5.19.1, the qualifier reads the published declaration
from the checksum-matched release JAR. It records the notice checksum and
the original scanner observation, with an unchanged upstream SPDX digest.
The assembled document reports `Apache-2.0 OR LGPL-2.1-or-later` as declared
and leaves the license conclusion unresolved for independent review. The
Story `REQ-C17-SPDX-COMPONENT-IDENTITY-001#spdx-retains-verified-jna-publisher-declarations`
covers both components, missing and conflicting notices, and tampering after
assembly. The canonical Linux archive verified all 225 files and 50 resolved
JARs. Evidence is under
`.refactorkit/runs/v080-c17-jna-publisher-declaration-20261120-r001/`.


[[c17-spdx-source-owned-replay-2026-11-19]]
=== Source-owned component replay for v0.8 release binding

The v0.8 workflow captures the application classpath with the repository
Gradle task. Finalization runs that task offline from the captured source
with a fresh destination, compares the replayed manifest with the supplied
one and checks the packaged JAR membership and SHA-256. The binding records
the replayed manifest digest alongside the independently verified SPDX.

The six-case Story exercises the same source-owned Gradle task in a fixture
checkout. It covers success and refuses changed coordinates, absent or stale
input, source drift and an archive with changed JAR bytes. A replay of the
sealed 6e6e archive also verified all 50 JARs. Evidence:
.refactorkit/runs/c17-spdx-source-binding-20261119-r001/.
Exact-source CI, license review and independent release acceptance remain
open for the final 0.8.0 candidate.


[[c17-v080-downloaded-asset-review-2026-11-19]]
=== Independent verification of downloaded Linux assets

The v0.8 release workflow delegates review of the downloaded build output
to a job with repository and attestation read permissions. The verifier
receives the expected repository, source revision and tag independently
of the asset set. GitHub CLI verifies provenance for the ZIP and evidence
binding, and the SPDX attestation for the ZIP. The verifier compares the
verified SPDX predicate with the downloaded document and checks its whole
file inventory against the archive and the evidence binding.

The runtime check executes the embedded CLI and MCP launcher from a
private copy. The CLI version must match the expected tag and API 0.2.
The draft job compares all four files with the review receipt from the
read-only job before creating the draft. Historic tags keep their
existing publication selection.

The operational Story uses a local attestation oracle and an executable
fixture for success and five refusal cases. It also checks the draft
handoff and rejects a changed SPDX download. The fixture cannot prove
remote signature verification. The same verification command can review
a separately downloaded draft or public asset set. The
link:../distribution-trust.md#independent-linux-v080-release-verification[download and runtime procedure]
uses a fresh asset set for each review and repeats the managed C relocation
fixture on the verified ZIP. Actual 0.8.0 attestations, draft and public
downloads remain release gates.
Evidence: .refactorkit/runs/c17-downloaded-release-verifier-20261119-r001/.
GitHub CLI policy options: https://cli.github.com/manual/gh_attestation_verify.


[[c16-c-signature-managed-lsp-2026-11-19]]
=== Managed C parameter insertion and reordering through LSP

The existing managed C LSP command previews, applies and rolls back explicit
parameter insertion and reordering for compiler-backed C11 and C17 fixtures.
The Story checks exact changes to the prototype, definition and caller, the
unchanged compilation database, and restoration of the source after rollback.
Two typed scalar-input refusals leave the workspace without a transaction.
All six cases and 24 steps pass in the isolated source tree.

A separate framed execution against the sealed 6e6e package verifies both
operations in both standards with exact source images and clean shutdown.
Evidence: .refactorkit/runs/c16-c-signature-managed-lsp-20261119-r001/
and .refactorkit/runs/c16-signature-lsp-readback-20261119-r001/.
Broader signature and release qualification remain open.

[[lsp-initialize-workspace]]
=== Select the workspace during LSP initialization

`REQ-LSP-INITIALIZE-WORKSPACE-001` admits the nullable root URI defined by
link:https://raw.githubusercontent.com/microsoft/language-server-protocol/gh-pages/_specifications/lsp/3.17/general/initialize.md[LSP 3.17].
An explicit file URI selects its workspace. A null or omitted root URI selects
the first supplied workspace folder. Initialization without either succeeds
with no workspace scan.

The link:../../features/lsp-initialize-workspace.feature[Story] checks
both null-root paths, explicit-root precedence and an omitted root URI. It
reads symbols through the public LSP dispatcher and verifies the two saved
sources byte for byte. The link:../integration-contracts.md#lsp-server-baseline[LSP integration contract]
documents the client boundary.
